  • "The Divining Runes of Merro Mosso" by Mario and Beto

Hopey goes on a picnic, to a rock 'n' roll show and the bathroom in "Saturday is Shatter Day," the latest installment of "Day by Day with Hopey." And on the Beto side of the book, "On a Gut Level" features the return on Palomar's original heartbreaker Pipo, trapped in a mysterious castle with Fritz, her ex Mark Hererra, and his wife Mila...plus another "Kid Stuff Kids"! VIVA LOS BROS!

Story Titles

  • "The Kid Stuff Kids" by Beto
  • "Day By Day with Hopey: Saturday is Shatterday" by Jaime
  • "Near Mint" by Jaime
  • "Angels of Tarzana" by Jaime
  • "On a Gut Level" by Beto

Ray is limp and sore and goes to a party with 40 guys and 3 girls. In "Day by Day with Hopey," Sunday is "Put Down That Gun Day" where the next day is school and she hasn't a thing to wear. On the Beto side of the book, Mark Herrera returns to giving self-help seminars in the big arenas, but how long will this last? In "Julio's Day," Julio's old schoolmate Araceli heads off to Viet Nam — will she return? And in the final installment of "The Kid Stuff Kids," we discover who mom is! Hint: Mom's a classic Palomar character.

Story Titles

  • "Fine To Very Fine" by Jaime
  • "Down in Heaven" starring the Kid Stuff Kids by Beto
  • "Day By Day with Hopey: Sunday is Put that Gun Down Day" by Jaime

Another outstanding issue of one of the most celebrated comics series ever! This time around, Jaime provides the concluding chapter of "Day by Day with Hopey," titled "Monday Ain't Just One Day": it's the first day of school for Hopey and the kids. Will she flunk like a skunk or soar to new heights? Be there or you'll be tardy and the principal will tan your hide. Gilbert in turn continues his prolific tradition with three stories: cult film star Fritz faces her father over a question of child abuse; Fritz's motivational speaker ex-husband Mark Herrera is invited to a mysterious exclusive club which may resurrect his fallen career; and in "Julio's Day," young Julio Juan discovers life in his new home isn't what you'd call comforting. We're counting down to issue 20 which will conclude the "Julio's Day" saga. Viva Los Bros!

Story Titles

  • "Blackouting" by Beto
  • "Day by Day with Hopey: Monday is Atilla the Hun Day" by Jaime
  • "Julio's Day" by Beto
  • "Day By Day with Hopey: Tuesday is...One More Tuesday!" by Jaime
  • "Dumb Solitaire: God's Eye-View"

The brothers that Time magazine called the next great storytelling innovators of this century are back with another captivating issue of Love and Rockets. In the last installment of Gilbert's "Dumb Solitaire" (the Mark Hererra saga), Mark makes a last ditch attempt to resurrect his career as a hip motivational speaker by hoping to re-marry his 4th ex-wife, Fritz (the now has-been B-movie star). Will she say yes? Or will she prefer to stay in her second marriage to Scott the Hog? In the second to last chapter of "Julio's Day," young Julio Juan lives out his gay dreams the way old Julio could never live out his own. On Jaime's side: Ray spends the day with the abominable Frogmouth and (along with you, dear reader) learns a few new things about her cockeyed life in "Tampas Pero No Trampan" — guest starring Angel of Tarzana. ¡Viva!

Story Titles

  • "Trampas Pero No Trampan"'by Jaime
  • "Pattern for Living" by Beto
  • "Julio's Day" by Beto
  • "Yes. God" by Beto

Don't get left behind as we gear up for the 20th-issue extravaganza! In the last chapters of "Julio's Day," Julio Juan settles into maturity and Aricela leaves for another mercy mission while old Julio's life reaches its twilight, inspiring him to reflect on the regrets and pleasures of the past as his 100th birthday approaches. We wouldn't be surprised if he met Fritz and had sex with her! (Just kidding.) Gilbert's "Emanon" is a silent, violent, oddly touching monster story. In Jaime's "Male Torso Found in L.A. River," Ray gets further drawn into Vivian's sordid, dangerous world (and Angel gets a taste of it as well) as one scumbag meets his fate at the wake of another scumbag. Later, Ray gets to watch while Viv and Angel skinny-dip and wrestle!

Story Titles

  • "Julio's Day" by Beto
  • "Male Torso Found In L.A. River" by Jaime
  • "Emanon" by Beto
  • "Uk Utirr Tagual Tor Zok", "Rocks Over Rocks" by Jaime
  • "Julio's Day" by Beto

Second great issue of the most acclaimed new series (and old series, for that matter!) of the last several years, and we're not just giving you corporate spin when we say we think you'll like this even better than the first issue. You can tell Los Bros are just warming up... In Beto's "Julio's Day," Julio goes to school, encounters bullies, difficult school work, attention deficit disorder and the slow destruction of passion and creativity by the school system. Mario & Gilbert deliver part two of "Me for the Unknown" â€“ a story filled with crooked politicians and revolution in the Comprachican bayou. And in Jaime's signature "Maggie," our heroine asks herself, "Does the world suck or do I suck? That is the question," while Izzy is still in her apartment and someone called The Frogmouth wants to be her best friend. Plus, the long-awaited return of Errata Stigmata in a short from Gilbert!

Story Titles

  • "Julio's Day" by Beto
  • "Maggie" by Jaime
  • "Me For The Unknown" by Mario and Beto
  • "Erratic Stigmata"
  • "Clip Art" featuring Roy and Natalia by Beto

If you missed Jaime Hernandez's "La Maggie La Loca" serial in the pages The New York Times, or even if you didn't, you can catch it in this special issue in an expanded "Director's Cut" format with the cuss words put back in and 4 added pages! Plus, seventeen-year-old Venus helps us say goodbye to Gilbert Hernandez's post-Palomar stories inLove & Rockets! Is "Venus and You" the swan song for those characters in L&R? Hmmm...

Story Titles

  • "La Maggie La Loca" by Jaime
  • "Venus and You"
  • "Pedro"
  • "Untitled"
  • "You People"
  • "The High Road" by Beto

Marked by Time magazine as one of the (well, more than one actually) top 100 innovators to look out for, Los Bros. Hernandez continue with the alternative series that started it all — this time, in Gilbert's "Julio's Day," Julio gets a break from the horrors of childhood and focuses on his sister Sofia's horrors: unrequited love, mysterious neighbors, and food poisoning; plus, his baby brother Benjamin is born — will he also live under Julio's unlucky star? In Jaime's new "Maggie" episode, Maggie and the Frog Mouth go sunbathing (yes: girls in bathing suits — life is good!), and whenever the Frog Mouth's around you never know what's going to happen! Finally, in the latest chapter of Mario and Gilbert's action thriller "Me for the Unknown," Lillard goes for a new identity with mixed results. Viva Los Bros. Hernandez!

Story Titles

  • "Maggie" by Jaime
  • "Julio's Day" by Beto
  • "Me For The Unknown" by Mario and Beto
  • "The Neuterbrank Primer" starring Roy, Errata and Natalia by Beto

Imaginary dogs roam its walkways at night. All the air conditioners are broken. The empty swimming pool is covered with flies. What does this all mean? Don't ask Maggie, the manager of the notorious Capri Apartments deep in the heart of the San Fernando Valley. She has no answers. She just wants it to stop being so damn hot. Izzy knows but she sure ain't telling. Over on Beto's side of the comic, in "Julio's Day," Julio watches as his little brother Benjamin becomes the scourge of the neighborhood, and in "26,280 Hours To Kill" our man Roy is wrongly imprisoned and the mother of all prison riots erupts. Plus the latest chapter of Beto + Mario's "Me for the Unknown"! Four stories from three Bros. add up to great entertainment!

Story Titles

  • "Me For The Unknown" by Mario and Beto
  • "Maggie" by Jaime
  • "Traditional Uses For a Corpse's Hand" starring Roy by Beto
  • "The Soft High Lisp" featuring Fritzi by Beto
  • "Maggie" by Jaime
  • "Julio's Day" by Beto
  • "The Frogmouth" featuring Ray D. and Vivian by Jaime

"Generations" might be the subtitle for this especially lively, eclectic, and time-spanning issue of Love and Rockets, timed to premiere on the title's 20th anniversary. In the lead story that flashes back way before even the original Love and Rockets #1, a seven-year-old Penny Century is introduced to a forty-something H.R. Costigan — her husband-to-be many years later. Meanwhile, back in the present, Hopey spends quality time with her daddy, and Ray plays a game of "Over the Line" with some old Hoppers partners. Gilbert picks up the issue's theme and runs with it in the latest installment of "Julio's Day," as we find out some things about Julio's parents that will surprise us. Also, "The High Soft Lisp" centers around Fritz's punk days and her hopeless infatuation with Scott the Hog, the lead singer of the original Love and Rockets (from the Love and Rockets X graphic novel)...plus the latest ripping installment of the Mario/Beto south-of-the-border thriller "Me for the Unknown"! Three cartoonists, six stories, one modern classic!

Story Titles

  • "Bay Of Threes" by Jaime
  • The story of H.R. Costigan and Penny
  • "Our Return"
  • "First Mexican on the Moon"
  • "Roy and Judith" by Beto
  • "Me For the Unknown" by Mario and Beto
  • "Confirmation" A Sister Mary Joseph story
  • "The Soft High Lisp"
  • "Julio's Day" by Beto

This issue of Love and Rockets reintroduces one of Gilbert's wackiest characters: Roy! This cover-featured tale is the mother of all Roy epics, as Roy is wrongfully imprisoned and then caught in a hellish jailbreak. Plus Julio's dad lays it down in this issue's installment of "Julio's Day," Dr. Fausto explores the mysterious case of "Rosario X," beloved Danish comedian Dirk Passer stars in a classic "Peterson" adventure, and a new chapter of the Beto/Mario adventure epic "Me For the Unknown." Over on the Jaime side of the fence, after last issue's Penny Century extravaganza, Maggie, Hopey, and Ray are back for three new stories!

Story Titles

  • "Toco" by Beto
  • "Maggie" by Jaime
  • "Kid Stuff" featuring Jimmy and Killer
  • "Julio's Day" by Beto
  • "30,000 Hours To Kill" A Roy Story
  • "Peterson" by Beto
  • "Me, For The Unknown" by Mario and Beto

This issue of Love and Rockets aims to surprise those faithful followers of Los Bros Hernandez. In Gilbert's "Julio's Day," the rain continues to pour down hard on Julio's life. Jobs become scarce so he and his brother Benjamin leave town to find work. Meanwhile, the stock market crashes in New York City. In "The High, Soft Lisp," the buxom Fritz re-hooks up with motivational speaker Mark Herrera in a most intimate way - they get married! And even nuttier, it's to each other! Big tits and the boners who love them is the order of the day in this neurotic installment. Meanwhile, Jaime delivers a story that picks up directly from the previous issue: Maggie and her new kissin' buddy "the Frogmouth" return to Hoppers to retrieve a stolen item from Izzy...and find more than they bargained for in the process! Viva L&R!

Story Titles

  • "Maggie" by Jaime
  • "Me For The Unknown" by Mario and Beto
  • "The Soft High Lisp" Featuring Fritzi and Mark by Beto
  • "Julio's Day" by Beto

What the hell is going on in Izzy's house? Maggie, Hopey, Doyle, and other recurring characters share reminiscences about the strange history of their strange friend's long-time residence in this issue's "Maggie" installment by Jaime Hernandez. Over in Beto-land, in "The High Soft Lisp," Fritz's happy marriage begins to unravel, and an over-the-top way to save it turns out to be the biggest mistake yet. And what might that be, you ask? Deranged sex! What else? Plus, in "Julio's Day," the rain won't let up, forcing Julio and his brother to find work out of town, and "Me for the Unknown" begins charging towards its climactic finale next issue. All this, plus more surprises.

Story Titles

  • "She's Only Crying" by Beto
  • "Maggie" by Jaime
  • "The Little Stunt Boy"
  • "Julio's Day"
  • "The Soft High Lisp" by Beto

In Jaime's half: Meet the Chascarrillos! Spend time with the most mysterious family in comics. There's our beloved Maggie, her wacky sister Esther, their goofy brothers Manuel, Angel and Ruben, and of course their classy mom Quina. Find out where Maggie gets it all. Where she learned to say "UTA." On Beto's side, Julio's mother worries about her two sons away working in the city — with all those wicked city women and all. In the concluding installment of "The High Soft Lisp," after Fritz's marriage fizzles she tries again and marries her dream of dreams — Scott the Hog! Plus the next-to-last chapter of the epic adventure "Me For the Unknown."

Story Titles

  • "Maggie" by Jaime
  • "The Soft High Lisp"
  • "Julio's Day" by Beto
  • "Me, For The Unknown" by Mario and Beto
